about: Reviewed source changes v1.0.11 did not ship: portability fixes for platforms it never compiled (fold step B6), and guard fixes that keep the compiled code identical (B8). files: each pinned to its reviewed bytes (layout-insensitive sha256 of the C/C++ tokens, equivalence.py closure_digest); level 1 and the closure check compare against that instead of the shipped bytes. objects_identical: Linux TUs whose tokens change but whose objects level 3 must find identical. token_deltas: the named TUs whose portable replacement changes Linux code on purpose, allowed at level 2.

runtime-recomp/src/game/achievements.cpp.reason: libc++ (Apple, Android) has no std::atomic<std::shared_ptr>; the published snapshot is a dkr::runtime::AtomicSnapshot (atomic_snapshot.hpp), which is that type wherever the standard library has it (libstdc++, MSVC) and falls back to the shared_ptr atomic free functions on libc++.

runtime-recomp/src/game/connection_ui.in.reason: The live Rollback panel reads experimental::runtime_view(), which runtime_ui.cpp declares only with DKR_EXPERIMENTAL_RACE_TEST; v1.0.11 always defined it, Apple builds do not. The panel is under the same condition (token-identical where it is defined).

runtime-recomp/src/game/f3ddkr_rt64.cpp.reason: Metal builds have no enhanced-water renderer; the water_residency_rt64.hpp include is skipped under __APPLE__ (token-identical elsewhere).

runtime-recomp/src/game/mod_store.cpp.reason: libc++ (Apple, Android) has no std::atomic<std::shared_ptr>; the published snapshot is a dkr::runtime::AtomicSnapshot (atomic_snapshot.hpp), which is that type wherever the standard library has it (libstdc++, MSVC) and falls back to the shared_ptr atomic free functions on libc++. Android links no HTTPS backend, so its curl include and backend are skipped there (the store reports itself unavailable).

runtime-recomp/src/game/mod_store_instal.reason: libc++ (Apple, Android) has no std::atomic<std::shared_ptr>; the published snapshot is a dkr::runtime::AtomicSnapshot (atomic_snapshot.hpp), which is that type wherever the standard library has it (libstdc++, MSVC) and falls back to the shared_ptr atomic free functions on libc++. libc++ file_clock counts are __int128, which std::to_string has no overload for; the count goes through std::int64_t, the overload libstdc++ already picked.

The TU now also reads that header; its preprocessed tokens are unchanged (level 2).
